title: One complete round of the width split
statement: Let $f:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, and let $C,D$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet with positive numbers of work tapes. Choose states $c_e,c_x$ of $C$ and $d_e,d_x$ of $D$, and let $w,s$ be Boolean words. Suppose $a,b>0$, the run of $C$ from its seam on input $w$ with $s$ on its first tape does not visit state $c_x$ at any time strictly between $0$ and $a$, and at time $a$ it is at state $c_x$ with the binary representation of $f(|s|)$ on its first tape. Suppose likewise that the run of $D$ from its seam on input $w$ with the suffix of $w$ after its first $|s|$ bits on its first tape does not visit $d_x$ strictly between times $0$ and $b$, and at time $b$ it is at $d_x$ with the binary representation of the suffix length on its first tape. Then the combined controller, started at its anchor with candidate $s$, has some time $t>0$ satisfying $t\le a+b+10(|s|+|w|+|u|+|v|+10)$, where $u$ and $v$ are those two binary output words. It avoids the anchor at every time strictly between $0$ and $t$; at time $t$ it is halted with output encoding the pair consisting of the prefix of $w$ of length $|s|$ and the remaining suffix if $|s|+f(|s|)=|w|$, and otherwise it is back at the anchor with candidate advanced by one bit when $|s|\le |w|$ and unchanged when $|s|>|w|$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a function from natural numbers to natural numbers
C and D are finite Boolean-alphabet Turing machines
C and D each have a positive number of work tapes
ce and cx are states of C
de and dx are states of D
w and s are Boolean words
a and b are positive natural numbers
C avoids cx at all times strictly between 0 and a from its stated seam configuration
C is at cx with first tape containing the binary representation of f(|s|) at time a
D avoids dx at all times strictly between 0 and b from its stated seam configuration
D is at dx with first tape containing the binary representation of the suffix length at time b
replaced:
Suppose the width call on the candidate $s$ returns the binary word of
$f(\abs{s})$ in $a > 0$ steps and the suffix-length call returns the binary
word of the suffix length in $b > 0$ steps, each with no interior
exit-state visit. Then there is a time $t$ with
$0 < t \le a + b + 10(\abs{s} + \abs{w} + \ell_u + \ell_v + 10)$, where
$\ell_u, \ell_v$ are the two binary words' lengths, such that the round
from the canonical anchored seam carrying $s$ never revisits the anchor
strictly between $0$ and $t$, and at time $t$: if
$\abs{s} + f(\abs{s}) = \abs{w}$ the controller has halted with output the
pair encoding of the split of $w$ at $\abs{s}$, and otherwise it is back at
the canonical anchored seam carrying the stepped candidate.
